title: Database Health
description: PostgreSQL (3 servers), Redis, VictoriaMetrics, Loki and Tempo: container caps and OOM kills, connections, throughput, cache and storage. Sources: Alloy's built-in postgres/redis exporters, podman-metrics.sh, and each store's own /metrics. Alerts in the database_health group mirror the top row.

panels.title: PostgreSQL reachable
panels.description: pg_up from Alloy's postgres exporter, one value per server.

panels.title: OOM kills, last 24h
panels.description: Processes killed by the kernel inside each container's cgroup (memory.events oom_kill). Unlike podman's OOMKilled flag this catches a single Postgres backend dying, which takes the whole server through crash recovery. Alert: ContainerOOMKill.

panels.title: Container memory, % of cgroup limit
panels.description: Usage divided by the container's own memory cap (podman stats). Alert ContainerMemoryNearLimit fires at 90% for 10m. postgres was OOM-killed at 100% of 512m on 2026-09-09; caps now: postgres 768m, litellm 1536m.

panels.title: PostgreSQL connections, % of max_connections
panels.description: Backends across all databases on each server versus its max_connections (100). Alert PostgresConnectionsHigh at 80% for 5m.

panels.title: Memory usage
panels.description: Resident memory per container. Compare with the caps in the bar gauge above; caps are not drawn here to keep one axis.

panels.title: OOM kills (10m increase)
panels.description: Same expression as the ContainerOOMKill alert.

panels.title: Restarts
panels.description: podman RestartCount. Rises when the restart policy brings a crashed container back (litellm looped 13 times on 2026-09-09).

panels.title: Connections by server
panels.description: All backends per server. max_connections is 100 on each.

panels.title: Transactions / s
panels.description: Commits and rollbacks per second. Rollbacks climbing without commits usually means an application error loop.

panels.title: Buffer cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of block reads served from shared_buffers. Sustained drops below ~0.95 mean the working set no longer fits in memory.

panels.title: Rows fetched / inserted / updated / deleted per s
Longest running transaction
panels.description: Oldest open transaction. Long idle-in-transaction sessions hold locks and block vacuum.

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: On-disk size per database (templates and the maintenance DB hidden).

panels.title: Dead tuples awaiting vacuum
panels.description: Rising steadily means autovacuum is not keeping up. Only tables visible to the exporter's role are counted.

panels.title: Temp file bytes / s
panels.description: Sorts and hashes spilling to disk because work_mem is too small for the query. The chat-search query that killed a backend on 2026-09-09 is the kind of thing that shows up here first.

panels.title: Checkpoints / h
panels.description: Requested checkpoints (as opposed to timed) mean WAL is filling faster than checkpoint_timeout; consider raising max_wal_size.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: maxmemory is unset on this instance, so the container's cgroup cap (see Containers row) is the real ceiling.

panels.title: Keyspace hits and misses / s
panels.description: Authentik uses this Redis as a Celery broker and session store rather than a lookup cache, so both counters sit at zero and a hit-ratio panel divided 0 by 0 and plotted nothing. Flat zero here is the expected state; a rising miss rate would mean something started doing cache lookups against it.

panels.title: Evicted keys and rejected connections (1h increase)
panels.description: Evictions mean memory pressure; rejected connections mean maxclients hit. Both should stay at zero.

panels.title: Neo4j (neo4j-pod, Community: metrics via cypher-shell collector)
Neo4j reachable
panels.description: neo4j-metrics ran RETURN 1 through cypher-shell in the last minute. Alert Neo4jDown after 2m.

panels.title: Active transactions
panels.description: Includes the collector's own transaction, so the floor is 1.

panels.title: Collector run time
panels.description: One JVM start of cypher-shell per minute. Alert Neo4jMetricsStale if no success for 5m.

panels.title: Store on disk
panels.description: databases = graph store; transactions = tx logs (retention policy 2 days 2G).

panels.title: JVM heap
panels.description: Alert Neo4jHeapHigh at 90% of max for 10m.

panels.title: GC time / s
panels.description: Fraction of wall time spent in each collector. Old-generation time rising means the heap is too small for the working set.

panels.title: Nodes by label
panels.description: Top 8 labels by count.

panels.title: Rows inserted / s
panels.description: Ingestion by source: promscrape (its own scrape jobs), prometheus remote write (Alloy), import (podman-metrics.sh, cron scripts).

panels.title: New series created / s
panels.description: Churn. A sustained rise usually means a label with unbounded values (ids, timestamps) slipped into a metric.

panels.title: Slow inserts and slow queries / s
Scrape targets
panels.description: VictoriaMetrics' own scrape jobs (vmscrape.yml). The litellm job was down from 2026-09-02 to 09-09 without anyone noticing; this is where it shows.

panels.title: Loki: lines and bytes received / s
Tempo: spans received / s
panels.description: Discarded spans mean the per-tenant ingestion limits in tempo-config.yml are being hit.
